verses.text: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.
The sons of Ham were: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before Yahweh. Therefore it is said, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Yahweh”.
The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Out of that land he went into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,
and Resen between Nineveh and the great city Calah.
Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim (which the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon (his firstborn), Heth,
the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad.
The border of the Canaanites was from Sidon — as you go toward Gerar — to Gaza — as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim — to Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, after their families, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.
Children were also born to Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth.
The sons of Shem were: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.
To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Their dwelling extended from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, by their families, according to their languages, lands, and nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these in the earth after the flood.

footnotes.content: After the waters receded, Noah's family becomes the seed from which the whole earth is again filled. I take heart that God's faithfulness to preserve a remnant is what gives us any hope at all. And that hope ultimately points us to the true and greater Remnant, our Lord Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Japheth scatter toward the coasts and islands, each with their own tongue and clan. I see the mercy of God spreading families abroad to fill the earth as He intended. Even in dispersion, the Lord is ordering the nations, and one day He will gather a people from every tribe and tongue to Himself in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ham's line stretches south and west, giving rise to many peoples. I am reminded that God's blessing rests not on the line of prominence, but on the line of promise. It is not Cush or Canaan who will ultimately bless the nations, but One born of Shem who will redeem them all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cush bears Nimrod, and the text says he 'began to be a mighty one in the earth'. I tremble at that word 'began' — not mighty in faith, but mighty in his own eyes. How different from Abraham, who was called a mighty man of faith by trusting the God who calls him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The proverb says, 'like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Yahweh'. The Hebrew suggests a hunter in defiance of Yahweh, not for Him. I need to ask my old heart whether I am hunting for glory before men, or humbling myself before the Lord who alone is glorious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh mark the cradle of Nimrod's kingdom, stretching into Assyria to build Nineveh and its great cities. I see man grasping for a name and a city apart from God. But our true city is not made by human hands — it is the city whose builder and maker is God, prepared for all who trust in Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mizraim's sons give rise to peoples who will later intersect with Israel's story, including the Philistines from Casluhim. I see how the Lord ordains these families long before their conflicts with His people. Even when nations rise against His covenant people, He remains faithful to keep every promise He has made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sidon is named first among Canaan's sons, and from him come the many tribes whose land God will one day give to Abraham's seed. I grieve that Canaan's line is marked for displacement because of their wickedness, yet I rejoice that God's covenant faithfulness to Abraham cannot fail. The borders drawn here only serve to highlight the greater inheritance God gives to those in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The writer pauses to say these are Ham's sons by families, languages, lands, and nations. I love that God sees each clan by its own tongue. He is not a God of vague humanity, but a God who knows and loves the peoples He has made — and has purposed to redeem a people from them all through Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shem is called 'the father of all the children of Eber', and here we see the line through which the blessing will run. I notice the order: Shem, the elder brother of Japheth in this listing, is the one through whom God will call Abram. It reminds me that God's purposes often turn on what seems least to the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram — names that will echo through Israel's history for good and ill. I am thankful that the God who numbers these families is the same God who has numbered every hair on the head of those who belong to His Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Arpachshad fathers Shelah, and Shelah fathers Eber, from whom come Peleg and Joktan. The name Peleg means 'division', for 'in his days the earth was divided'. I wonder at God's mercy in dividing tongues and lands to curb the pride we saw at Babel. He restrains our sin to give us time to repent and turn to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joktan's sons spread far to the east, with names that stretch toward Arabia and beyond. I am struck that God's plan includes every corner of the earth from the very beginning. The gospel would one day reach even the most distant of these families, bought by the blood of Jesus Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their dwelling goes from Mesha toward Sephar, to the mountain of the east. These are simple markers of homes and hearths, yet each represents image-bearers loved by God. I rest in the truth that our Lord knows every tribe by name and has died to redeem them for Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again the refrain: families, languages, lands, and nations. I see the Lord delighting in the diversity He created, even as He calls all of it back to Himself. In Christ, our differences need not divide us — they become a reason to marvel at the grace that saves people from every nation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations divided from these families after the flood. This long genealogy ends where it must: pointing us beyond the nations to the One who will bless all nations. After all these names, my heart longs for the day when every knee bows and every tongue confesses that Jesus Christ is Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
